subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this custom cooperative glob traversal and an event-loop turn between sequential `agent:bootstrap` hook handlers as canonical internal behavior?
rationale: The reviewed head has no discrete correctness defect and preserves public SDK signatures, but these filesystem-parity and scheduling choices are long-lived compatibility-sensitive contracts that focused tests and green CI cannot authorize.

options.title: Adopt both contracts
options.body: Refresh against current main and merge because the real liveness proof and focused parity coverage are sufficient for these internal contracts.

options.title: Split hook scheduling
options.body: Land asynchronous bootstrap reads and cooperative glob traversal now, then review inter-handler yielding in a smaller follow-up.

options.title: Narrow to async reads
options.body: Keep only the guarded asynchronous root-file reads if maintainers do not want to own the custom walker contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt both contracts
recommendation.body: Refresh against current main and merge because the real liveness proof and focused parity coverage are sufficient for these internal contracts.
